recommendation: Keep the human-review audit unless a human can recover Archive.zip and identify a concrete current-source defect. Reconcile any recovered row as a precise issue against the affected active resource source rather than applying speculative bulk QA edits.
issue_request: FHIR-17609 is a Published/Persuasive Patient Care technical correction from the STU3 QA issue pool. It asks editors to check an attached Archive.zip of QA review files and records the accepted resolution as "Auto approved typos", with no comments, related artifacts, or specific source paths beyond FHIR-core-many.
initial_application: No current source marker or available git commit explicitly mentions FHIR-17609. Historical untagged Patient Care QA commits after the issue was filed, especially 8af82e04026d1c904036e5c48529d6d93387c295 and f4a82c18ac26d814f93407d27e1b1a617fc3478a, changed Linkage, Communication, ClinicalImpression, and multiple Patient Care terminology/resource files, suggesting broad historical QA application without row-level traceability.
additional_context: The current build still includes active Patient Care resources touched by those historical QA commits. The Jira attachment URL for Archive.zip returns HTTP 403, the Jira snapshot has no row detail or comments, and direct FHIR-17609 source, Zulip, and Confluence searches found no issue-specific evidence. Broader QA-family evidence shows these 2018 QA bundles had many fixed and orphaned rows and were later treated as old relevance-review material.
reconciliation: No source files were changed. The issue is too broad and attachment-dependent to safely translate into a current build edit without the underlying QA rows, and the available evidence does not identify a concrete current typo or semantic defect.
